message.content: The sea typically looks blue—because water absorbs colors at the red end of the spectrum and scatters the shorter blue wavelengths—but its hue can shift. In shallow, clear waters it may appear turquoise or greenish, while deeper or murkier seas can look darker blue or even black. Algae, sediment, and the angle of sunlight also influence how we perceive its color.
